content.comment_body: Hello everyone, We had a [product_name] operator display [article_no] in our inventory since 2010. I decided to use it for an application and unpacked it for the first time about an hour ago. After connecting the display as instructed, the LCD only shows a blank screen with all pixels dark; however, the backlight works and immediately upon powering up, for a brief moment, there's a message: FW V1.05.06 before the display returns to black. The function keys I programmed are working as planned—I can observe their responses through the online monitor in [product_name] software tool. No other keys work. Any advice?

Hi, Could you attach your program file (zipped) so we can check the configuration? I doubt this is the cause, but it's worth checking. Also, please specify the [product_name] module type ([article_no]) and the version numbers for both the [product_name] and display. Regards,

Thank you for responding quickly. I'm certain the program isn't the issue. I suspect the display itself is faulty. Viewing the display from a wide angle reveals that text is actually being shown. It's behaving as if the contrast is set to maximum. I managed to access the contrast settings menu, but the contrast level won't change. I can navigate the menus but only if I view the screen at a steep angle, over 150 degrees.

Hi, It appears you're correct: the [product_name] display is defective. You could submit a support request for assistance, which is free, but likely you'll need to send the display in for repair. Regards,

Thank you. I've identified the issue. The fault lies with the ST7565 chip located beneath the LCD. I'll attempt to replace the chip if feasible, or else install a new LCD display, which should cost less than 10 Euros. Thanks for your support.

Hi, If you have the necessary skills and equipment to swap the display driver, it's worth the effort. Personally, I wouldn't recommend using it for a customer, but for your own use it's acceptable. Best of luck. Regards,
Yes, I possess the tools and expertise required. I'm curious how a device bearing two 'Quality control passed' labels could be faulty immediately upon opening the package.

analysis.insight_summary: A user encountered a non-functional [product_name] display module right after unpacking, despite it having quality control approval labels. The LCD exhibits all pixels active except for a quick firmware message at startup. Some functions are accessible via the system software, but normal display operation is impossible. The experience raised doubts about product quality control reliability and caused user frustration.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expected the [product_name] operator display module to work properly out of the box with no hardware or display faults, given it had passed quality control.
